title: Restructure Admin Configuration for category navigation and dirty state
description:
Problem: the continued `/admin` Configuration review found the tab rendering as a very long single settings surface on narrow width, with more than 160 inputs, more than 50 switches, and repeated per-setting Save buttons. The page is searchable, but the current layout makes category scanning, dirty-state awareness, and save scope hard to understand.

Desired outcome: Admin Configuration should feel like a managed settings workbench: searchable, categorized, compact, and explicit about what changed and what will be saved.

Scope:
- In scope: category navigation, sticky compact filters, setting grouping, dirty-state indicators, save scope, repeated Save button reduction, keyboard/focus flow, and responsive rendering of setting descriptions/keys.
- Out of scope: changing the allowlisted settings catalog or persistence backend unless needed to expose dirty-state metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
- Operators can jump between setting categories without scrolling through the entire catalog.
- Changed settings are visually identifiable before save.
- Save actions make their scope clear and avoid dozens of visually identical buttons in the first-pass scan.
- Setting keys/descriptions are readable but do not dominate the narrow layout.

Validation:
- Capture `/admin` Configuration before/after at narrow and desktop widths with default and filtered states.
- Run focused browser checks for search, category selection, changing a switch/text setting, dirty-state display, save, and cancel/reset behavior.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 continued live review: Admin Configuration measured as a very long single settings panel with 164 inputs, 52 switches, and many repeated Save controls on narrow width.
